lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fábia | Lesson 9 -- Twelve Point Five

listenings.text: Right, the quarter. Revenue was one million four hundred and eighty thousand. Margin, twenty-two percent. Overhead came in at four hundred and twelve thousand. Headcount cost, two hundred and sixty-eight thousand. And the variance against budget was eighty thousand. That is the quarter. Any questions before I move on to the next client?

Let me take the four lines in order. Revenue closed at one point four eight million, which is nine percent higher than the second quarter, and about eighty thousand ahead of forecast. The margin is where it gets interesting: twenty-two percent, three points lower than a year ago, and that is on higher revenue, which is unusual. The reason is the third line. Overhead is up twelve and a half percent, the highest it has been since twenty twenty-three, and two thirds of that increase is the new warehouse alone. Against the sector benchmark we are still slightly better than average, but not by much. So the line to watch next quarter is the warehouse, not the margin.

matching.title: Match the word to its meaning
defs: all the money a business takes in, before costs
what is left after you take the costs away
what you expect the numbers to be, before they happen
the difference between the plan and what really happened
the standard number you compare yourself against
the cost of running the business, whatever you sell

items.situation: Revenue is 1,480,000. Last quarter it was 1,360,000. One sentence.
Margin is 22% now and was 25% a year ago. Say it without sounding defensive.
Overhead is the biggest it has been in three years.
tips: the highest it has been since ...
up twelve and a half percent

items.situation: The client asks: "Is twelve days good?" Compare it with the sector.
Close the report: name the one line to watch, and why.
tips: because two thirds of it is ...

arguebank.label: Useful language
items: B has more information and less meaning.
Twenty numbers with nothing to compare them with.
In A I know where to look in ten seconds.
A figure on its own is not analysis.
The client is paying for the comparison, not the ledger.
B is what a system prints. A is what a person says.
There is one client for whom B works: ...
What is missing from B is ...
A tells me the line to watch.
